questions.stemHtml: A psychotic patient, 3 days after taking haloperidol, presented with acute dystonia of neck muscles. The best drug for managing this condition is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Benzhexol
  • Haloperidol is a D2 blocker, which may produce acute dystonia when started.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 290

questions.stem: A Patient on antipsychotic therapy for 1 month develops a feeling of restlessness, frequently repetitive, stereotyped movements, and an inability to sit still for more than a short period. Which of the following drug is responsible for this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Haloperidol
  • The clinical features point towards Akathesia.
  • Akathesia is an Extrapyramidal syndrome Characterised by a feeling of restlessness, frequently repetitive, stereotyped movements, and an inability to sit still for more than a short period.
  • It occurs due to longtime intake of antipsychotics like Haloperidol which block D2 and cause Extrapyramidal symptoms.
  • The treatment approved is propranolol and benzodiazepines.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 290

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man presents with schizophrenia and Tardive dyskinesia. which of the following is the most appropriate drug treatment:
questions.solutionHtml:
Clozapine

Analyze The Question:

  • The patient has tardive dyskinesia and schizophrenia.
  • Tardive dyskinesia is due to typical antipsychotics, and to overcome this side effect, you need to shift to an atypical antipsychotic like clozapine which doesn't produce tardive dyskinesia.
  • Tardive dyskinesia is because of long-term d2 blockade.
  • If they specifically ask you to manage only tardive dyskinesia, valproate will be the answer.
  • Droperidol and chlorpromazine are typical antipsychotics, and they cause tardive dyskinesia.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 290

questions.stem: A 20-year-old male patient was started on an atypical antipsychotic. The drug dose was increased to bring the disease under control. After a few months, his blood levels showed increased prolactin levels. Which was the drug given to this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Risperidone
  • Atypical antipsychotic
  • Becomes "typical" at high doses leading to eps (>6mg)
  • Blocks selective d2, so it causes maximum hyperprolactinemia
  • Long-acting injectable formulation
  • Shares sedation, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, and elevated prolactin
  • No agranulocytosis risks
  • More hyperprolactinemia

Note:

  • Among Atypical Antipsychotics Risperidone, Paliperidone Have High D2 Affinity And Blocks It Causing Hyperprolactinemia


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 12th Edition, Page Number: 423

questions.stem: A drug used for Schizophrenia has 98% first-pass metabolism when given as an oral tablet. So the drug is available as an oral dissolving tablet to avoid pass effects. The atypical antipsychotic is given by sublingual route:
questions.solutionHtml:
Asenapine
  • Atypical antipsychotic given by sublingual route is asenapine
  • It is available only as an ODT preparation administered sublingually, and absorption occurs via the oral mucosa with a bioavailability of 35%
  • If asenapine is swallowed, the first-pass effect is greater than 98%, and the drug is not bioavailable.
  • Intramuscular administration avoids much of the first-pass enteric metabolism and
  • Provides measurable concentrations in plasma within 15–30 min

questions.solutionHtml:

questions.stem: A 30-year-old patient was started on lithium carbonate for bipolar disorder. The nurse will give instructions on the adverse effects of the therapy. The patient should report back if the following features are seen:

options.label: A
options.text: Palpitations, chest pain, raised blood pressure

questions.solutionHtml:
Tinnitus, severe diarrhea, ataxia
  • Adverse effects of lithium
  • The Mnemonic “ fell hen”
  • All- alopecia, acne
  • F – fine Tremor (MC), teratogenicity
  • E - Ebstein’s anomaly
  • L – Leucocytosis
  • L – loose stools(diarrhea)
  • H – Hypothyroidism
  • H – high dose( Tinnitus, coarse tremors, coma, and convulsions)
  • E- ECG Changes(Reversible elevation of T waves)
  • N- Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus

questions.stem: Hemodialysis is advised following an acute overdose of lithium if lithium has the following blood concentration:
questions.solutionHtml:
> 3 mEq/L
  • Dialysis is the most effective means of removing Li + and is necessary for severe poisonings, that is, in patients exhibiting symptoms of toxicity or patients with serum Li + concentrations of 3 mEq/L or greater in acute overdoses

questions.stem: Lithium is effective in acute mania but not used as a single agent in the management of acute mania because:

options.label: B
options.text: 5-7 days are required for clinical effect

options.label: D
options.text: Binds to plasma proteins so not available for immediate action

questions.answerText: 5-7 days are required for clinical effect
questions.solutionHtml:
5-7 days are required for clinical effect
  • Lithium is effective for mania but not used as a single agent in the management of acute mania because 5-7 days are required for clinical effect
  • Until that we need to add atypical antipsychotics like olanzapine to control the mania
  • Benzodiazepines may be used as adjuvant PK points you need to remember
  • Completely absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract
  • Does not bind to plasma proteins
  • Not metabolized
  • Eliminated by the kidneys, sweat, saliva, breast milk and tears
  • Half-life approximately 24 hours
  • Steady-state concentrations reached within 5 days
  • Na depletion leads to lithium retention--toxicity

questions.stem: A 24-year-old male patient of Schizophrenia came withAn inexpressive or blank face ( flat affect)Monosyllabic speechLack of gesturing when communicatingLack of eye contact andPhysical inactivity.What would be the drug of choice for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Clozapine
  • This patient has negative symptoms of Schizophrenia
  • The Drug of choice for Negative Symptoms is Clozapine.
  • Haloperidol is the preferred drug for acute schizophrenia.
  • Loxapine is a Dibenzoxazepine having CPZ-like DA blocking and antipsychotic activity.
  • There is no clear-cut advantage over other antipsychotics.
  • Pimozide is a selective DA antagonist with little Alpha-adrenergic or cholinergic blocking activity.
  • Because of the long duration of action (several days; elimination t½ 48-60 hours) after a single oral dose, it is considered good for maintenance therapy but not when psychomotor agitation is prominent.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 468,469,470

questions.stem: A 54-year-old female patient on an antipsychotic drug develops jaundice and Abdominal pain. Investigations done revealedHb-11.4 g/dL LFT SGOT-46 IU/L SGPT-42 IU/L Bilirubin Total – 2.2 mg/dL Bilirubin Indirect – 0.6 mg/dL Bilirubin Direct – 1.8mg/dL Which of the following Anti-psychotic medications lead to this derangement ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chlorpromazine
  • From the presentation of a patient with jaundice and raised Bilirubin with an increase in Direct bilirubin > indirect Bilirubin, we can infer that the patient has a rise in Conjugated Bilirubin.
  • Chlorpromazine causes Obstructive jaundice and, therefore can present with the following derangements.
  • Jaundice is rare with Haloperidol.
  • Clozapine and Flupenthixol also do not cause jaundice .


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology,By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 467,468

questions.stem: A 32-year-old male patient with Schizophrenia who was on Haloperidol medication developed restlessness within 2 weeks of treatment and kept pacing back and forth in his room. He also developed tremors in his hand. What is the preferred drug for controlling restlessness in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Propranolol
  • In case of Anti-psychotic induced restlessness(Akathisia), the drugs that are given for controlling it are Propranolol, Diphenhydramine, Clonazepam, Lorazepam, Benztropine, etc.
  • Valbenazine is the DOC in Tardive dyskinesia.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man on Antipsychotics complains of sedation. Which of the following Antipsychotics is least likely to cause it?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ziprasidone
  • Ziprasidone Haloperidol, Chlorpromazine, and Thioridazine are drugs that cause sedation in patients.
  • Ziprasidone may cause mild sedation, but it is not a major side effect, as seen with the other 3 drugs mentioned.
  • The aliphatic and piperidine side chain phenothiazines (CPZ, triflupromazine, thioridazine) have low potency, produce more sedation, and cause greater potentiation of hypnotics, opioids, etc.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 470

questions.stem: A Patient on starting a particular drug develops High fever, muscle rigidity, unstable BP, etc. He was diagnosed to have Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. Which of the following drugs would not lead to this effect?
questions.solutionHtml:
Amantadine
  • Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome is said to be because of Dopamine receptor antagonism.
  • Amantadine shows D2 receptor agonism by increasing Dopamine presynaptically.
  • Metoclopramide, Haloperidol, and Domperidone have D2 receptor antagonistic action and, therefore, can lead to Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 290

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl is brought to the psychiatry OP by her mother as she notices the child havingThroat clearingSniffingGrunting and alsoBlinkingEye dartingFacial grimacingShoulder shruggingNose twitching etc. occasionally.You diagnose the child to have Tourette’s syndrome. Which of these drugs is preferred in Tourette’s syndrome?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aripiprazole
  • Aripiprazole is the only antipsychotic that is FDA approved for the treatment of Tourette disorder, first line agent.
  • Tourette’s syndrome is characterized by multiple motor or phonic tics (which may be awkward or obscene) prevalent mostly among children .
  • It is treated symptomatically with behavioural therapy and training.
  • It is often supplemented by typical antipsychotic drugs, especially haloperidol or pimozide. Atypical antipsychotics like risperidone and aripiprazole have also been found to help overcome compulsive tics.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 473

questions.stemHtml: A 56-year-old patient taking Anti-psychotic medication came to the casualty with light headedness, syncope and a sensation of pounding heartbeat . ECG was taken and it showed the following change. Which of the following drugs is least likely to lead to this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Clozapine
  • This patient has Long QT syndrome which can lead to Arrhythmia.
  • Clozapine has the least chance of leading to QT prolongation among the given drugs.
  • High doses of Thioridazine
  • Ziprasidone
  • Pimozide directly depress the heart and produce ECG changes (Q-T prolongation and suppression of T wave). They exert some antiarrhythmic action, probably due to membrane stabilization.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 466,475
